title: Onboarding Toolchain Access and Career Checkpoints
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook documents the standard onboarding toolchain, the recommended access matrix by role, and the career progression checkpoints that People Ops and managers should use during the first 12 months. The goal is to reduce friction for new hires, make access predictable (time-to-provision target = 48 hours for core tools), and align early work with clear growth milestones.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: All full-time employees and long-term contractors at Redwood Inference. Includes hosted product teams and platform/infrastructure teams.
- Audience: Hiring managers, people-ops, IT/tooling engineers, team leads, and new hires.

Quick summary / SLAs:
- Standard provisioning SLA: 48 business hours for core tools (Okta, Slack, GitHub, GCP/Azure/AWS read access, Confluence).
- Elevated access (admin credentials, production secrets): additional approvals required; target: 5 business days.
- Escalation: people-ops on-call -> IT tooling group -> Security (if access requested to production secrets).

Access matrix (selected tools):
| Role | Okta Groups | GitHub | Slack | Cloud Console | Datadog | Vault | JIRA | Notes |
| Engineer (IC-1/IC-2) | engineering-core | repo:write | team-channel | project:dev-readonly | viewer | env/dev | dev-projects | Standard dev access for feature work |
| Engineer (IC-3+) | engineering-core, engineering-sre | repo:write, infra:read | multiple-team-channels | project:dev, project:staging | monitor | env/staging | dev+prod-projects | Require manager approval for prod access |
| Product Manager | product-core | repo:read | product-team | project:analytics-readonly | dashboard-read | env/none | product-projects | Access to analytics and product repos |
| SRE / Infra Eng | infra | infra-admin | infra-channel | project:prod-admin | admin | env/prod | ops-projects | Requires 2FA + security training completion |
| People Ops | people-ops | org-admin (non-code) | hr-channel | billing-read | n/a | env/none | onboarding-projects | Access to HR and billing consoles |

Provisioning checklist (step-by-step, manager + new hire):
1. Hire accepted: manager creates 'New Hire Request' in the Onboarding Tracker (confluence template).
2. People Ops creates initial Okta user and assigns role group.
3. Tooling bot ticket auto-generated for GitHub, Slack, JIRA, Cloud enrollment.
4. New hire completes security orientation and 2FA enrollment before access to staging/prod.
5. Manager verifies access within 48 hours and logs any missing items on the ticket.
6. After week 2, tooling engineer closes provisioning ticket and moves the user to regular access review cadence.

Week-by-week starter checklist (first 90 days):
- Week 0 (pre-boarding): account invites, reading list, manager 1:1 scheduled, hardware shipped.
- Week 1: Slack intros, Confluence reading: team charter, codebase overview, dev environment setup, run the example local service.
- Week 2: First small bug/patch merged, join team standups, complete security checklist.
- Week 4: Shadow a production incident review or release playbook.
- Week 8: Deliver first small feature or telemetry improvement.
- Week 12: Career checkpoint 1 — manager and new hire review progress against role expectations.

Career progression checkpoints (manager-guided):
- First checkpoint (90 days): Demonstrates core competency for role level (code quality, communication, shipping small features). Manager evidence: PRs merged, peer feedback, onboarding tasks completed.
- Second checkpoint (6 months): Ownership of a meaningful feature or technical area. Demonstrates problem decomposition and cross-team collaboration.
- Third checkpoint (12 months): Ready for promotion consideration if consistently exceeding expectations; evidence includes impact metrics, mentoring newer hires, and improving process.

Promotion readiness signals (non-exhaustive):
- IC-1 -> IC-2: Consistent independent delivery on medium-sized tasks, reliable testing and observability.
- IC-2 -> IC-3: Ownership of end-to-end feature, influence on design, reliable mentoring.
- Engineering manager early signals: stakeholder communication, project planning, 1:1s conducted, coaching evidence.

Access request and escalation process:
1. Use the 'Tool Access Request' form (Confluence link in related resources). Include justification, duration, and manager approval.
2. Automated checks run: 2FA status, security training completion, current role groups.
3. If automated checks pass, provisioning proceeds. If not, ticket assigned to people-ops.
4. For production or admin access: require explicit security approval (Security reviewer + Team lead).
5. If SLA breached ( > 48 hours for core tools), escalate to people-ops lead and cc manager.

Tooling ownership and contacts:
- Okta / SSO / HR sync: People Ops Identity Team (identity@redwood.ai) — SLAs and group design.
- GitHub org and repo management: Platform Tooling (platform-tools@redwood.ai).
- Cloud accounts and billing: Cloud Ops (cloud-ops@redwood.ai).
- Secrets / Vault: Security Infra (security-infra@redwood.ai).

Policy notes and security controls:
- 2FA required for all employees on all corporate accounts.
- Use of personal devices for production access requires company-approved endpoint security; see Endpoint Security policy.
- Admin keys and long-lived secrets are prohibited; require ephemeral session token workflow.

Manager guidance for 1:1 career checkpoints:
- Bring evidence: PR links, demo, feedback from peers.
- Use rubric: technical execution, communication, product impact, autonom y.
- Set measurable goals for the next checkpoint (eg. own a feature, ship a performance improvement, mentor new hire).

Frequently asked questions (FAQ):
Q: How long for production DB access?
A: Typical timeline 5 business days after security approval and completion of required runbook training.

Q: Who approves org-level GitHub admin rights?
A: Platform Tooling + Security must both approve; require justification and rotation plan.

Change log and ownership:
- Owner: People Ops (People Ops Identity Team). For changes to roles or SLA, the owner must coordinate with Security and Platform Tooling.
- Change record: 2025-09-15 created by Aisha Patel; 2026-02-10 updated to tighten provisioning SLA and add career checkpoints.

Appendix: common Okta group names and meanings:
- engineering-core: standard engineering access group
- infra: infra team membership (higher privileges)
- product-core: product and PM access group
- people-ops: HR/People Ops access

End of document.
